$comment: events.watch -> POST calendar/v3/calendars/{calendarId}/events/watch, request Channel, response Channel. The action a subscription trigger's `create` names: the HOST calls it with a fresh channel id, its own URL and the connection's channelToken, and reads the lease from the response's `expiration` (epoch MILLISECONDS, as a string). Google: "there's no automatic way to renew a notification channel" -- so it is also what the host calls again when the lease is due.
title: Google Calendar watch
description: Open a push-notification channel on a calendar's events. The host's subscription machinery calls this; it is not a node most workflows need.
$idempotencyComment: Google offers no idempotency key on events.watch. A retried call with the SAME channel id is refused (the id must be unique), and with a fresh id it opens a SECOND channel that delivers duplicates until it expires. Honestly unsafe-to-replay; the host stops a channel it is not sure about.

constants.$comment: The only delivery type Google offers for Calendar. A literal, so it cannot be misspelled per call.

config.label: Calendar ID
config.description: `primary` for the connected account's own calendar, or a calendar's id.

config.label: Channel ID
config.description: A UUID the host mints for THIS channel. Google requires it to be unique; it comes back in every notification as X-Goog-Channel-ID and is what channel_stop needs.

config.label: Notification URL
config.description: The HTTPS URL the host mounts for this trigger. Google POSTs notifications here with an EMPTY body and the facts in X-Goog-* headers.

config.label: Channel token
config.description: The connection's channelToken. The host fills this from the connection -- never type a value here. Google echoes it in X-Goog-Channel-Token, and that echo is how a delivery is verified.
config.$comment: A CREDENTIAL sent in the body, which no earlier provider needed and the vocabulary has no word for yet -- authorize places the primary credential and `also` adds headers, and nothing writes a credential into a JSON body. Graph's clientState is the same shape, so the two-provider bar for `request.fromCredentials` is met; until it exists the host passes the value as config. Recorded in .ai/plans/vocabulary-deferred.md.

config.label: Lifetime (seconds)
config.description: How long Google keeps the channel alive. Google's default is 604800 (one week), and the discovery document types it as a STRING inside `params`.
config.$comment: A string, not a number: `params` is a map<string,string> in the discovery document, and a JSON number there is refused. Nested `as`, because it lives under params.

outputShape.description: The channel id -- what was sent.
Google's opaque id for the watched resource. channel_stop needs it together with the channel id.
The token that will be echoed on every notification.
When the channel expires, as epoch MILLISECONDS in a string. The subscription trigger's lease is built from this.
Which estate this ran against. Google has no sandbox, so: fake or live.
